scaleBeatText: With Haven grieving, Ashford installs their own speaker at the table. Tribute rises to 7,500 kcal/week. Grief is leverage, and they know it. The link holds — it was never with one person.
🗣️ Wei to Nikolai, by the fire: "The table's set. The ring of pale light — it's just sitting there. Waiting on them. What do you think they'll tell it?"
🚶 Haven walks from the table cleanly — no blades, no hard words. The bond ends where it stood, honestly.

With Haven grieving, Stonebridge installs their own speaker at the table — but the bond is young, and they're still deciding what Haven is. The new speaker wants to talk before the tribute changes. Grief delays the verdict: send grain (1,500 kcal), send a speaker (2 days), or let the silence answer.

Seven days of silence, and the silence answered for Haven. Stonebridge's new speaker reads it plainly. (Trust -6.) Stonebridge installs their own speaker at the table after all — tribute rises to 7,500 kcal/week. Grief became leverage, and they knew it would.
Word comes: Stonebridge's speaker is dead. In the chaos, Haven renegotiates — tribute down to 5,625 kcal/week. The link holds: it was never with one person. They grieve; the gains wait.
◈ THE TABLE IS SET. A ring of pale light waits — take your seat from Haven when you are ready. Nothing is final until you sit.
With Haven grieving, Stonebridge installs their own speaker at the table. Tribute rises to 8,438 kcal/week. Grief is leverage, and they know it. The link holds — it was never with one person.
◈ OVERTIME ×1 — wave 4–5 monsters return as RERUNS (+25% HP, +12% damage). Raids come sooner. The table docks your standing −13. Take your seat from Haven to stop the clock.

With Haven grieving again, Stonebridge installs their own speaker at the table — and reaches for the grief card once more. The table has heard it before: the grief card is spent. Tribute stays at 8,438 kcal/week. The link holds — it was never with one person.

📜 Oliver's book stays open on the table: one promise unkept — Grace — help Grace with their sickness — they're feverish, a cut gone hot and angry. The promises died with his maker; the needs didn't. What you do about them is yours to decide.
